summary: No substantive defect established in the inspected empirical design and mathematical decomposition. Explicit latent recovery need not ensure a correct learned predictor. Report clarifies query-scale risk, task/architecture limits, and specific exceptions rather than treating the paper as an impossibility theorem.
limitations: No author code release in frozen packet; no empirical reproduction.
No universal architectural impossibility or exhaustive absence-of-latents inference.
Selected tables/figures only; external biological/task provenance not audited.
title: Does learning the right latent variables necessarily improve in-context learning?
acceptance_scope: NoIssueFound scope independently checked against report/coverage and original pp7-8. The source explicitly distinguishes learned predictor failure from latent inference, uses a newly trained known-decoder oracle, acknowledges difficult nonlinear latents, compares direct versus decoded auxiliary loss, and gives the Figure7 shortcut-training exception. The report correctly preserves these controls and task/architecture limits rather than claiming an impossibility theorem or absence of latents. The conditional identity E[(x^T e)^2|e]=sigma^2||e||^2 requires independent fresh query and latent error; tripled query scale gives9-fold risk but does not remove between-model comparisons. No raw runs, code, split integrity, statistical significance or exhaustive figure audit is newly certified.
